title: Wrong VLAN on Access Port
symptom: PC1 and PC2 are supposed to be in the same VLAN but cannot ping each other even though they have IPs in the same subnet.
device_context: Cisco 2960 switch SW1. PC1 is on Fa0/1 and PC2 is on Fa0/2. Both should be in VLAN 10.
expected_fault: PC2 on Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 10. That is why PC1 and PC2 cannot communicate.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# interface Fa0/2
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10

title: VLAN Does Not Exist in Database
symptom: Ports Fa0/3 and Fa0/4 are configured for VLAN 20 but hosts connected to them cannot send any traffic.
device_context: Cisco 2960 switch SW1. VLAN 20 is assigned to Fa0/3 and Fa0/4 but VLAN 20 was never created.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 does not exist in the VLAN database. Ports assigned to a non-existent VLAN become inactive.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# vlan 20
SW1(config-vlan)# name SALES
SW1(config-vlan)# exit

title: VLAN Missing from Trunk Allowed List
symptom: VLAN 30 users on SW1 can talk to each other but cannot reach VLAN 30 users on SW2. All other VLANs work fine between the two switches.
topology: PC5 -> Fa0/5 (SW1) | PC6 -> Fa0/5 (SW2) | SW1 Gi0/1 -- trunk -- Gi0/1 SW2
device_context: Cisco 2960 switches SW1 and SW2 connected via Gi0/1 trunk link. VLAN 30 exists on both switches but is excluded from the trunk.
show_output:
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1       1-29,31-4094

Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1       1,10,20
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is not in the allowed VLAN list on the trunk. Frames tagged with VLAN 30 are dropped at the trunk port.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# interface Gi0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30

SW2(config)# interface Gi0/1
SW2(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30

title: Access Port Set to Trunk Mode
symptom: A PC connected to Fa0/10 cannot get a DHCP address and cannot pass traffic. The port shows as trunk instead of access.
device_context: Cisco 2960 switch SW1. Fa0/10 should be an access port in VLAN 10 for a regular PC but was accidentally configured as a trunk.
show_output:
Name: Fa0/10
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: trunk
Administrative Trunking Encapsulation: dot1q
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Fa0/10 is in trunk mode. A regular PC cannot handle 802.1Q tags so it receives no valid frames and cannot get a DHCP address.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# interface Fa0/10
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10

title: Wrong Default Gateway on PC
symptom: PC1 (192.168.10.5/24) can ping all PCs in the same subnet but cannot reach any device outside the subnet.
device_context: PC1 has a static IP with gateway set to 192.168.10.100 which does not exist. The correct gateway is 192.168.10.1.
show_commands: show ip interface brief (on router R1)
show_output:
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
FastEthernet0/0        192.168.10.1    YES manual up                    up
FastEthernet0/1        192.168.20.1    YES manual up                    up
expected_fault: PC1 has the wrong default gateway configured (192.168.10.100). No router exists at that address so off-subnet traffic cannot be forwarded.
expected_fix: On PC1: Change default gateway from 192.168.10.100 to 192.168.10.1

title: Missing Static Route
symptom: R1 can reach the 192.168.10.0/24 network but cannot reach 192.168.30.0/24 even though R2 is the next hop and is reachable.
device_context: Cisco routers R1 and R2 connected via 10.0.0.0/30. R1 has no route to 192.168.30.0/24.
show_output:
Codes: C - connected, S - static, R - RIP

Gateway of last resort is not set

C    192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, Fa0/0
C    10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Se0/0
expected_fault: R1 has no route to the 192.168.30.0/24 network. Packets destined for that subnet are dropped because R1 does not know how to forward them.

title: OSPF Neighbor Not Forming
symptom: Two routers R1 and R2 are connected but OSPF neighbor relationship is stuck in INIT or DOWN state. No routes are being exchanged.
device_context: Cisco routers R1 and R2. OSPF is configured on both but R1 is in area 0 and R2 is in area 1 on the same link.
show_output:
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
(no output - no neighbors listed)
expected_fault: R1 and R2 have mismatched OSPF area numbers on the connected interface. OSPF neighbors must be in the same area to form an adjacency.
expected_fix:
R2(config)# router ospf 1
R2(config-router)# no network 172.16.0.0 0.0.0.255 area 1
R2(config-router)# network 172.16.0.0 0.0.0.255 area 0

title: OSPF Hello Timer Mismatch
symptom: OSPF neighbor relationship keeps going down and coming back up. The link is stable but the adjacency is flapping.
device_context: Cisco routers R1 and R2. OSPF hello interval on R1 is 10 seconds (default) but on R2 it was manually set to 5 seconds.
show_output:
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
Internet Address 192.168.1.1/30, Area 0
Hello interval 10, Dead interval 40
Neighbor Count is 0, Adjacent neighbor count is 0
expected_fault: OSPF hello timers do not match between R1 and R2. Routers must have the same hello and dead intervals to maintain a stable adjacency.
expected_fix:
R2(config)# interface Gi0/0
R2(config-if)# ip ospf hello-interval 10
R2(config-if)# ip ospf dead-interval 40

title: RIP Version Mismatch
symptom: R1 and R2 are running RIP but are not exchanging routing updates. Both have RIP configured but no routes appear in the routing table.
topology: R1 Se0/0 -- serial link -- Se0/0 R2
device_context: Cisco routers R1 using RIP version 1 and R2 using RIP version 2. RIPv1 and RIPv2 are not compatible in this setup.
show_output:
Routing Protocol is RIP
Version 1
Sending updates every 30 seconds
Invalid after 180 seconds
expected_fault: R1 is running RIP version 1 and R2 is running RIP version 2. RIPv1 does not understand version 2 updates and vice versa in this case.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# router rip
R1(config-router)# version 2

title: Default Route Not Advertised in OSPF
symptom: All routers in the OSPF domain can reach each other but none can reach the Internet. The edge router R1 has a default route but it is not shared with other routers.
device_context: Cisco routers running OSPF. R1 has a default route via ISP but it is not redistributed into OSPF so other routers have no Internet route.
show_output:
Codes: O - OSPF, C - connected

O    192.168.10.0/24 [110/2] via 10.0.0.1
C    10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Gi0/0

(no default route entry)
expected_fault: R1 has a default route but it is not being advertised into OSPF. Other routers do not know how to reach the Internet.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# router ospf 1
R1(config-router)# default-information originate

title: ACL Blocking Valid Traffic
symptom: PC1 in 192.168.10.0/24 cannot reach the web server at 192.168.20.10 on port 80. All other traffic is working fine.
device_context: Cisco router R1 with an inbound ACL on Fa0/0. The ACL is too restrictive and blocks HTTP traffic from PC1.
show_output:
Extended IP access list 101
10 deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.20.10 eq 80 (25 matches)
20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL 101 explicitly denies TCP port 80 from the 192.168.10.0/24 network to the web server before the permit statement applies.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# ip access-list extended 101
R1(config-ext-nacl)# no 10
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 10 permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.20.10 eq 80

title: ACL Applied in Wrong Direction
symptom: An ACL was created to block traffic from outside coming into the network but it is accidentally blocking internal users from going out.
topology: PC1 (internal) -> R1 (Fa0/0 = inside, Fa0/1 = outside) -> Internet
device_context: Cisco router R1. The ACL meant to filter inbound Internet traffic was applied outbound on the wrong interface.
show_output:
FastEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
Outbound  access list is 110
Inbound   access list is not set
expected_fault: ACL 110 is applied outbound on the inside interface (Fa0/0) instead of inbound on the outside interface (Fa0/1). It is filtering traffic leaving the internal network.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# interface Fa0/0
R1(config-if)# no ip access-group 110 out
R1(config)# interface Fa0/1
R1(config-if)# ip access-group 110 in

title: Implicit Deny Blocking All Traffic
symptom: After applying an ACL to allow only SSH access, all other traffic including ICMP and HTTP stopped working for all users.
device_context: Cisco router R1. An ACL was added to allow only SSH (port 22) traffic. The implicit deny any any at the end blocks everything else.
show_output:
Standard IP access list 10
10 permit tcp any any eq 22 (5 matches)
expected_fault: The ACL only permits SSH. Due to the implicit deny at the end of every ACL, all other traffic (ICMP, HTTP, etc.) is blocked.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# ip access-list extended 10
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 20 permit icmp any any
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 30 permit tcp any any eq 80
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 40 permit tcp any any eq 443

title: NAT Pool Exhausted
symptom: Internal users were able to reach the Internet earlier in the day but now many users are getting connection timeouts. Some users still work fine.
device_context: Cisco router R1 doing NAT with a small pool of 5 public IPs. More than 5 users are trying to access the Internet simultaneously.
expected_fault: The NAT pool only has 5 IP addresses and all are in use. New connection requests from other internal hosts cannot be translated.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# ip nat pool PUBLIC_POOL 203.0.113.1 203.0.113.20 netmask 255.255.255.0
(or switch to PAT / overload to share one IP across many users)
R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 interface Fa0/1 overload

title: PAT Not Configured on Correct Interface
symptom: Internal users cannot reach the Internet. The NAT translation command references an interface but it is the inside interface not the outside one.
topology: PCs -> R1 (Fa0/0 inside, Fa0/1 outside) -> ISP
device_context: Cisco router R1. PAT is configured but the overload is pointed at Fa0/0 (inside) instead of Fa0/1 (outside public IP).
show_output:
ip nat inside source list 1 interface FastEthernet0/0 overload
interface FastEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
 ip nat inside
interface FastEthernet0/1
 ip address 203.0.113.1 255.255.255.252
 ip nat outside
expected_fault: PAT is using the inside interface (Fa0/0) for translation instead of the outside interface (Fa0/1). Translated packets carry a private IP as source which is invalid on the Internet.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# no ip nat inside source list 1 interface FastEthernet0/0 overload
R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 interface FastEthernet0/1 overload

title: Unintended Root Bridge Elected
symptom: Traffic between two switches is taking a long slow path. An old cheap switch in the network has become the root bridge for Spanning Tree.
topology: SW1 -- SW2 -- SW3 (old switch, low bridge priority)
device_context: Three Cisco switches connected in a triangle. SW3 is an old 2950 with default priority 32768 but it has the lowest MAC address so it won the root election.
show_output:
VLAN0001
  Root ID    Priority    32769
             Address     0000.0000.0001 (SW3)
  This bridge is the root

  Bridge ID  Priority    32769
             Address     0000.aaaa.0001 (SW1)
expected_fault: SW3 became the root bridge because it had the lowest MAC address with the same default priority. This results in suboptimal traffic paths.
expected_fix: SW1(config)# spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 4096

title: Port Stuck in Blocking State
symptom: A host connected to Fa0/5 on SW2 cannot reach the network. The port is connected and the link light is on but no traffic passes.
topology: PC -> Fa0/5 (SW2) | SW2 is connected to SW1 which is root
device_context: Cisco 2960 switch SW2. Fa0/5 is a non-root port blocked by Spanning Tree because STP thinks there is a loop.
show_output:
VLAN0001
  Role Sts Cost      Prio.Nbr Type
  ---- --- --------- -------- ----------------
  Desg FWD 19        128.1    P2p    (Fa0/1)
  Root FWD 19        128.2    P2p    (Fa0/2)
  Desg BLK 19        128.5    P2p    (Fa0/5)
expected_fault: Fa0/5 is in blocking state because STP detected a loop or the port lost a root port election. The host cannot send traffic on a blocked port.
expected_fix:
SW2(config)# interface Fa0/5
SW2(config-if)# spanning-tree portfast
(Use PortFast only on ports connected to end devices, not switches)

title: PortFast Enabled on Trunk Port
symptom: After enabling PortFast on all ports for faster convergence, a loop formed in the network causing a broadcast storm.
device_context: Cisco switches. A network admin enabled PortFast on all interfaces including Gi0/1 which is a trunk link to another switch.
show_output:
VLAN0001
  Port info      port id         128.1
  Role           Desg Sts        FWD
  Link-type      P2p  Peer (STP) has port in PortFast mode

(broadcast storm occurring)
expected_fault: PortFast was enabled on a trunk port connecting to another switch. PortFast skips STP listening and learning states so a loop formed immediately.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# interface Gi0/1
SW1(config-if)# no spanning-tree portfast
(PortFast should only be on ports connected to end hosts)

title: Telnet Enabled Instead of SSH
symptom: The network admin needs to connect to the router remotely but the connection is unencrypted. Password is visible in packet capture.
device_context: Cisco router R1 with VTY lines configured for Telnet only. SSH is not enabled so all management traffic goes over the network in plaintext.
show_output:
Line       Mtty Uses Noise  Overruns  Int
 0 vty 0     0    1    0       0/0       -
 1 vty 1     0    0    0       0/0       -
 2 vty 2     0    0    0       0/0       -

Transport Input: telnet
expected_fault: VTY lines are configured to accept Telnet only. Telnet sends all data including usernames and passwords in plaintext.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# ip domain-name company.local
R1(config)# crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048
R1(config)# line vty 0 4
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
R1(config-line)# login local

title: Console Port Has No Password
symptom: Anyone with physical access to the router console port can log in without a password. This is a basic security misconfiguration.
topology: Local access via console cable to R1
device_context: Cisco router R1. The console line has no password configured. The login command was also not set so the device accepts blank password.
show_output:
Line       Mtty Uses Noise  Overruns  Int
 0 con 0    -    1    0       0/0       -

Password: (not set)
Login: (not set)
expected_fault: No password is set on the console line. An attacker or unauthorized person with physical access can directly enter privileged mode.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# line console 0
R1(config-line)# password cisco123
R1(config-line)# login

title: DHCP Pool Configured on Wrong Subnet
symptom: Hosts on the 192.168.20.0/24 network are not getting IP addresses. The DHCP server on R1 has a pool but it is configured for the wrong subnet.
device_context: Cisco router R1 acting as DHCP server. The DHCP pool is configured for 192.168.10.0/24 but the client segment is 192.168.20.0/24.
show_output:
Pool LAN_POOL :
 Network         : 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
 Default router  : 192.168.10.1
 Lease           : 1 days 0 hours 0 minutes
expected_fault: The DHCP pool is for the 192.168.10.0/24 network but clients are on 192.168.20.0/24. Offers do not match the client subnet so clients get no IP.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# no ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
R1(config-dhcp)# network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0
R1(config-dhcp)# default-router 192.168.20.1
R1(config-dhcp)# dns-server 8.8.8.8

title: DHCP Excluded Range Not Set
symptom: The router itself (192.168.10.1) and a static server (192.168.10.2) are getting IP conflicts because DHCP is handing out those addresses to clients.
topology: PCs -> SW1 -> R1 (DHCP server) | Server at 192.168.10.2
device_context: Cisco router R1 acting as DHCP server for 192.168.10.0/24. The first few addresses are used by network devices but not excluded from the pool.
show_output:
IP address        Detection method   Detection time
192.168.10.1      Gratuitous ARP     Aug 20 10:15:32
192.168.10.2      Gratuitous ARP     Aug 20 10:16:04
expected_fault: DHCP is assigning 192.168.10.1 and 192.168.10.2 to clients. These addresses are already used by the router and a static server causing IP conflicts.
expected_fix: R1(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10

title: DHCP Helper Address Not Configured
symptom: PCs on the remote 192.168.30.0/24 subnet cannot get an IP address. The DHCP server is on a different subnet at 192.168.10.2.
device_context: Cisco router R2 is the gateway for the 192.168.30.0/24 subnet. DHCP requests are broadcast and do not cross router boundaries by default.
show_output:
FastEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet address is 192.168.30.1/24
  Broadcast address is 255.255.255.255
  Helper address is not set
expected_fault: DHCP broadcasts from clients cannot cross R2 to reach the DHCP server. The ip helper-address command is needed to forward DHCP requests as unicast.
expected_fix:
R2(config)# interface Fa0/0
R2(config-if)# ip helper-address 192.168.10.2

title: Interface Shutdown
symptom: A router interface shows as administratively down. The connected segment has no network access.
topology: PC segment -> R1 Gi0/1 (down) -> Core network
device_context: Cisco router R1. Interface Gi0/1 was shut down either intentionally or by accident. Hosts on that segment lose connectivity.
show_output:
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0    192.168.10.1    YES manual up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/1    192.168.20.1    YES manual administratively down down
expected_fault: Gi0/1 is in administratively down state which means someone ran the shutdown command. It needs a no shutdown command to bring it back up.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# interface Gi0/1
R1(config-if)# no shutdown

title: Duplex Mismatch Causing Slow Performance
symptom: A server connected to SW1 can communicate but the connection is very slow and shows many errors. The link negotiated at half duplex on one side.
device_context: Cisco 2960 switch SW1. The server NIC is hardcoded to full duplex but the switch port was set to half duplex causing a mismatch.
show_output:
FastEthernet0/24 is up, line protocol is up
  Half-duplex, 100Mb/s
  Input errors: 345, CRC: 120, Frame: 0, Runts: 15
  Output errors: 0, Collisions: 280
expected_fault: Fa0/24 is operating at half duplex while the server expects full duplex. This causes late collisions and CRC errors leading to poor performance.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# interface Fa0/24
SW1(config-if)# duplex full
SW1(config-if)# speed 100

title: Wrong Subnet Mask on Router Interface
symptom: R1 and R2 are directly connected but cannot ping each other. The link addresses are in different subnets due to a subnet mask typo.
device_context: Cisco routers R1 and R2 connected back to back. R1 uses /30 mask and R2 uses /29 mask on the same link.
show_output:
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status     Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0    10.0.0.2        YES manual up          up

show run int Gi0/0:
 ip address 10.0.0.2 255.255.255.248  (/29)
expected_fault: R2 has a /29 mask (255.255.255.248) while R1 has a /30 mask (255.255.255.252). They are in different network ranges so they cannot communicate directly.
expected_fix:
R2(config)# interface Gi0/0
R2(config-if)# ip address 10.0.0.2 255.255.255.252

title: Wrong SSID or Password on Client
symptom: A laptop cannot connect to the company Wi-Fi network. Other devices on the same network work fine. The laptop shows authentication failure.
device_context: Cisco wireless access point configured with SSID CompanyNet and WPA2 password. The laptop has a saved profile with an old incorrect password.
show_output: (no output - no client associations listed for the laptop MAC address)
expected_fault: The laptop is failing WPA2 authentication because it has an incorrect password saved. The AP rejects the association request.
expected_fix: On the laptop: Forget the saved Wi-Fi network and reconnect using the correct SSID (CompanyNet) and current WPA2 password.

title: DNS Server Unreachable
symptom: Users can ping IP addresses (e.g. 8.8.8.8) successfully but cannot browse websites by name. Browser shows DNS resolution failure.
device_context: PC configured with DNS server 192.168.10.53. That DNS server is down or unreachable. DNS queries time out.
show_output:
Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=20ms TTL=55
Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=18ms TTL=55

ping companydns.local (from PC):
Request timed out.
expected_fault: The DNS server at 192.168.10.53 is unreachable. IP connectivity works but name resolution fails because DNS queries cannot reach the server.
expected_fix: On PC: Change DNS server to 8.8.8.8 (Google DNS) or 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare DNS) as a temporary fix. Investigate why 192.168.10.53 is down.

title: Inter-VLAN Routing Not Working
symptom: PCs in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 cannot communicate with each other even though they are on the same switch. Both VLANs exist and ports are correctly assigned.
device_context: Cisco 2960 switch SW1 connected to router R1 via Gi0/1 trunk. R1 has subinterfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 but the trunk is not configured on SW1.
show_output: (no output - no trunk ports listed on SW1 Gi0/1)
expected_fault: The link between SW1 and R1 is not configured as a trunk on the switch side. VLAN-tagged frames from R1 are not accepted so inter-VLAN routing fails.
expected_fix:
SW1(config)# interface Gi0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q

title: Enable Password Not Set
symptom: When a user connects via Telnet and enters the enable command to access privileged mode, the router prompts for a password but there is none configured. The router then refuses entry.
topology: Admin PC -> Telnet -> R1 VTY -> R1 enable mode
device_context: Cisco router R1. VTY lines have a password for basic login but no enable password or enable secret was configured. Users cannot reach privileged exec mode.
show_output: (no enable password or enable secret line found in config)
expected_fault: No enable password or enable secret is configured. The router cannot verify the user for privileged mode access and blocks the enable command.
expected_fix:
R1(config)# enable secret strongpassword123
(Use enable secret instead of enable password because secret uses MD5 hashing)
